page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 Intel CPU architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating at 2 threads per core. The processor hardware configuration includes an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 2 MB, and an L3 cache of 260 MB. Hardware capabilities feature vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including Intel AVX, AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel AMX tile and int8 execution units, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation ratio. It features no local NVMe SSD storage and no integrated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average single-core CPU execution, as indicated by Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests. However, overall multi-core computational throughput, PassMark CPU scores, and uncached memory bandwidth sit in lower performance percentiles due to the two physical core capacity. Measured network and workload metrics include static web serving throughput of 7.0 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation rates of 92.48 tokens per second.

By delivering a high memory-to-core ratio of 32 GB across 4 vCPUs, the n4-highmem-4 offers efficient resource allocation for memory-bound tasks that do not require high multi-threaded processing power. This configuration reduces overall compute overhead for memory-heavy deployments, avoiding unnecessary vCPU scaling to access additional system RAM. The server is suited for workload profiles such as in-memory caching systems, static web application serving, lightweight database management, and memory-bound background processing jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel cores and 32 GB of system RAM. Featuring an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and a large 260 MB L3 cache, it supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reveal average single-core CPU execution and static web serving speeds of 7.0 GB/sec, alongside average small-model LLM text generation performance, though multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth metrics remain lower due to the physical core limit. The server provides a cost-effective option for memory-heavy workloads without requiring higher CPU counts, making it suitable for standard in-memory caching, web serving, and lightweight database management.
